subject: general
question: The process of seeping of water into the ground is known as _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**infiltration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infiltration** is the process through which water enters the **soil's ground surface**.
 
• An instrument called an infiltrometer is used to measure the rate of water penetration into the soil.
 
• Water on the ground surface infiltrates the soil through infiltration. It is widely utilized in the fields of hydrology and soil science.
 
• The greatest rate of infiltration is described as infiltration capability.
 
• It is most commonly measured in meters per day, however, other units of distance over time can be used if necessary.
 
• As the moisture content of the soil surface layers increases, the infiltration capacity of the soil decreases. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aquifers **are layers of rock and/or sediment that store groundwater. The term "groundwater" refers to precipitation that has entered the soil below the surface and accumulated in voids underground.
 
• **A well **is an excavation or structure dug, driven, or drilled into the ground to access liquid resources, most commonly water.
 
• **Bawris **is an old technique for managing rainwater. These are deep wells dug into the ground with steps leading up to the stored water.
